Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week — good conversation. Security team follow-up: we need explicit confirmation of Redwood's backup purge cadence and an option for a temporary extension while we complete our legal hold review. Specifically:  
- What is the default purge cadence for point-in-time backups that may contain user-submitted content?
- Are there separate retention windows for audit logs vs. request logs vs. debug logs?
- Can Redwood provide a one-time snapshot retention extension (90/180/365 days) for accounts under a signed exception?
- Please include an up-to-date subprocessor list and confirm whether any backups are stored or processed outside of the US (we have cross-border transfer requirements).

Can you also attach SOC 2 evidence and the DPA addendum we should sign for a temporary exception? We need this by EOD Nov 30 to finalize the procurement path.

Regards,

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear list. Putting options on the table below and copying Legal (Laura) and Platform (Nikhil) so we can confirm the operational constraints.

Summary (default behavior):
- Point-in-time backups: rolling 30-day purge for standard hosted accounts (snapshots held for recovery, then removed).
- Audit logs: retained 365 days by default (immutable audit store).
- Request/metadata logs: retained 90 days by default.
- Debug/tracing logs: 30 days by default (rotated).

Temporary exception options (subject to contract addendum):
- Option A: 90-day snapshot extension (no config change; flag on account)
- Option B: 180-day snapshot retention (requires dedicated contract & limited to one-year pilot)
- Option C: 365-day extended retention (requires Dedicated capacity or VPC deployment + signed addendum)

Cross-border & subprocessors:
- We'll attach the current subprocessor list. Most backups are stored in the customer-region preferred cloud region; however, some operational snapshots used for failover may be replicated to our US/EU DR region depending on customer region policy.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to confirm legal hold language + DPA addendum text we can sign quickly.
2) Nikhil to confirm whether we can enable a 180-day snapshot flag for MedConnect on hosted accounts or whether Dedicated is required.
3) I will share the retention schedule and subprocessor PDF now.

Attachments: redwood_retention_schedule_v1.pdf, dpa_subprocessor_list_202611.pdf

Thanks — we can do a quick call if you want to walk through options.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Camila — quick legal note and proposed addendum language below. Forwarding to Hannah for clarity.

Legal hold / exception approach (proposed):
- Redwood will provide a temporary retention exception in writing for a specified account id and time window. Exceptions are bound to a signed DPA addendum that defines scope, duration, and export rights.
- For audit purposes, we will deliver a retention manifest and an export of relevant metadata (not full PII payloads unless otherwise specified in the addendum).
- Exception approval path: Sales -> Legal -> Security -> Ops. We will require a PO or signed contract (Deal ID noted) before enabling multi-month snapshot retention.

Retention recommendations (to reduce risk):
- Audit logs: keep at 365 days (no change).
- Request logs (e.g., API request/response metadata): propose 180 days for MedConnect under exception.
- Debug/trace logs: propose 90 days — we can mask or obfuscate PII if you need longer retention.

Subprocessor update: we need to send MedConnect the attested subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors operate outside the US for your account. Camila, please confirm whether any backup replication to EU region is enabled for this account.

I'll draft a short DPA addendum and route for signature.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Hannah / Tom — quick follow-up with concrete options after chatting with Eng and Legal. Apologies for the weekend note; we wanted to keep your EOD timeline.

Confirmed operational constraints:
- We can enable a 180-day snapshot retention for your account while you finalize legal hold review, but it requires a signed DPA addendum and confirmation of Deal ID/PO. This will be an account-level flag for hosted accounts and will increase snapshot storage costs (we'll provide a cost estimate in the PO).
- 365-day retention for all backups requires Dedicated or VPC deployment (we can pursue that path if you want a longer-term solution).
- No backups are routinely stored outside the US for US accounts; we do replicate to our EU DR region only when explicitly configured by the customer for cross-region failover.

Action items: 
1) If MedConnect accepts Option B (180 days), provide the Deal ID or PO and we'll circulate the addendum via DocuSign (link below).
2) Laura will attach the final DPA addendum language.
3) Nikhil will produce an export manifest of snapshot identifiers and the audit log hashes for the retention window once the addendum is signed.

Cost estimate: we will follow up with a short line-item sheet once you confirm Option B.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call to finalize if easier.
